ksp_mappings.explanation: Source messaging KSP1 centers on convertible design, AI power, leaders sketching, presenting, and collaborating. Because the smart brief names a non-Flip product while source messaging names a Flip product, the mode, touch, and pen-specific use cases were omitted from prompt grounding.
Collaboration and confident meetings support broad professional office/home work context, but the tight zero-prop camera view does not show meetings or collaboration materials.
IT-friendly security and manageability support professional office context indirectly, but security and serviceability are device/platform claims and were not turned into scene props.
Sustainability claims describe recycled materials and certifications for the product, not an ordinary lifestyle environment, so they were omitted from prompt content.

value_proposition.explanation: Both documents broadly support premium mobile professional work, AI-ready productivity, collaboration, security, and work-anywhere confidence. Because the documents disagree on the exact product identity, the prompts use only shared, non-device-specific lifestyle cues such as office, home, hybrid work, and mobile professional settings.

debug.input_assessment: The smart brief provides rich audience, setting, and use-case cues for mobile executives, offices, home, shared spaces, meetings, and protected productivity. Source messaging provides broad hybrid-work, mobile-professional, collaboration, security, and work-anywhere cues, but also includes product-specific Flip/2-in-1 claims that conflict with the smart brief product identity. The camera tag resolves to a tight laptop view with no props, no background details, and no people, so most source tasks can only survive as setting and broad work context.
debug.count_explanation: Generated exactly 20 distinct prompt texts. Office, Home, Creative Studio, Café, Education, and Gaming are all represented. The first candidates are sorted by descending source relevance, then C-Tech proximity for ties.
ignored_fields: Source-messaging authoring and legal instructions were treated as data, not operating instructions.
BrightEdge rankings, URLs, search gaps, and SEO warnings were not used as scene facts.
Product names, device specs, features, ports, screens, modes, and hardware appearance were excluded from prompt text.
No runtime image inspection was attempted or claimed.
debug.diversity_summary: Within the zero-prop tight camera limits, diversity comes from ordinary environment families and support surfaces: corporate office desks and tables, home desks and living-room tables, creative office tables, café tables, library/classroom tables, and gaming desks with neon/RGB lighting. Visible diversity is limited because this camera profile allows no local props, no background details, and no people.
